name: Kyiv
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Kyiv: reconstruction partner diligence, ownership tracing, sanctions screening and dispute support.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Kyiv, scoped from Nashville: due diligence on Ukrainian partners in reconstruction, defence and energy projects, ownership tracing through Kyiv-registered holding companies, and factual support for counsel before Kyiv courts and the city's international arbitration institution, all under sanctions screening.
intro: Kyiv is Ukraine's capital and its economic, political and administrative centre, with a population of around 3 million in 2022. It is the seat of national authorities and the registered home of a majority of the country's strongest companies, including state energy groups such as Energoatom, Naftogaz and Ukrnafta. Kyiv registered more new businesses than any region in 2025, 34,655 entrepreneurs and companies. The full-scale Russian invasion has placed considerable strain on the city's economy, yet IT, food processing, pharmaceuticals, construction and a fast-growing defence and drone sector remain active, and reconstruction demand continues. Businesses surveyed by the National Bank in late 2025 named military action and shortages of qualified staff as their main constraints.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Kyiv because most large Ukrainian contracts, ownership structures and financing decisions run through the capital. Development lenders, contractors and investors entering reconstruction, energy or defence supply projects need to know who stands behind Kyiv-registered counterparties and whether any have links to sanctioned persons. Ownership of many groups still runs through Cyprus, Netherlands or other offshore holdings, and wartime asset seizures and nationalisations have changed control of some businesses. Procurement integrity is a priority for donors. Counsel in commercial disputes, arbitration and recovery work need well-sourced facts on counterparties and assets that may now be located inside or outside Ukraine.

matters.title: Reconstruction contractor and partner diligence
matters.text: Background research on Kyiv-based contractors, engineering firms and consultants bidding for donor-funded or government reconstruction work, covering ownership, management, prior contracts, litigation and adverse media, so lenders, joint venture partners and funders can assess capacity, conflicts of interest and integrity before committing funds.

matters.title: Sanctions-sensitive ownership tracing
matters.text: Mapping the shareholders and controllers of Kyiv-registered companies through Ukrainian registers, court records and foreign holding company filings to identify any connection to persons sanctioned by the United States, European Union, United Kingdom or Ukraine, including interests restructured or placed under state management since 2022.

matters.title: Defence and dual-use supplier vetting
matters.text: Research on Kyiv technology and drone manufacturers and their suppliers before investment, licensing or procurement relationships, covering ownership, founders' backgrounds, component sourcing claims and any history of export control issues, scoped carefully around security-sensitive information that should not be collected or held.

matters.title: Energy and state enterprise counterparties
matters.text: Fact-finding on companies trading with or contracting for Kyiv-headquartered state energy groups, testing ownership links to officials, prior anti-corruption proceedings and procurement disputes, to support compliance reviews by international suppliers, lenders and insurers working in Ukraine's power and gas sectors.

matters.title: Dispute, arbitration and asset research
matters.text: Assembling factual records for counsel in commercial litigation, ICAC arbitration or recovery actions involving Kyiv parties, including related companies, published court decisions, registered property where accessible, and assets located abroad that may be relevant to security, enforcement or recognition proceedings.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Kyiv
local_context.text: Ukraine's commercial courts operate on three levels, with the Commercial Cassation Court inside the Supreme Court at the top. The Supreme Court, the High Anti-Corruption Court and the city's first-instance and appellate commercial courts all sit in Kyiv. The Kyiv Appellate Court hears applications to recognise foreign arbitral awards and challenges to awards from arbitrations seated in Kyiv. Electronic filing and online hearings are available, which makes court records an important source for dispute research.

local_context.title: International Commercial Arbitration Court
local_context.text: The International Commercial Arbitration Court at the Ukrainian Chamber of Commerce and Industry is governed by the 1994 Law of Ukraine on International Commercial Arbitration, its Statute and its Rules. It is seated in Kyiv at 33 Velyka Zhytomyrska Street, and the place of arbitration under its rules is Kyiv, although hearings may be held elsewhere by agreement. It remains Ukraine's principal institution for cross-border commercial disputes.

local_context.title: Wartime operating conditions
local_context.text: Martial law has applied since February 2022. Some public registers have been restricted or partially reopened during the war, sanctions and state management measures have changed control of certain businesses, and air raids and power disruption affect working patterns. In the National Bank's late-2025 survey of Kyiv companies, military action and shortages of qualified staff were the leading constraints. Research timetables, field steps and source availability must be planned around these conditions.

local_context.title: Capital-city concentration
local_context.text: Because ministries, regulators, the National Bank and the headquarters of most major banks and state enterprises are in Kyiv, decisions about procurement, licensing and financing for projects across Ukraine are typically taken in the capital. Registered addresses in Kyiv often reflect head offices rather than the location of assets, so diligence should follow operations, plants and land into the regions where they actually sit.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Kyiv, TDSC begins with a sanctions screening and jurisdictional review, because as a US company it does not accept engagements that would violate US or other applicable sanctions, and some Kyiv counterparties have Russian-linked histories. Research is carried out from Nashville using Ukrainian company and court records as currently accessible, anti-corruption and procurement publications, foreign registries for holding companies, and Ukrainian-language media. Where field enquiries or document retrieval are justified, TDSC coordinates with qualified Ukrainian professionals and the client's counsel, with security considerations built into the plan. TDSC avoids collecting security-sensitive information and limits personal data to what the purpose requires.

faqs.q: Can you research Kyiv companies while martial law restricts some registers?
faqs.a: Yes, with limits that we explain at the outset. Access to certain Ukrainian registers has been restricted and partially restored during the war, so we combine what is currently available with court decisions, procurement data, foreign registry filings and media archives. Where a gap matters to the decision, we discuss lawful options with the client's Ukrainian counsel rather than working around restrictions.

faqs.q: How do you check whether a Kyiv counterparty has links to sanctioned Russian interests?
faqs.a: We trace shareholders and controllers through Ukrainian and foreign records, review sanctions lists maintained by the United States, European Union, United Kingdom and Ukraine, and look for historical ownership that was restructured after 2014 or 2022. We distinguish documented links from allegations and recommend that counsel review any match before the client acts on it.

faqs.q: Do you support donors and lenders on reconstruction procurement in Kyiv?
faqs.a: We conduct integrity due diligence on bidders, subcontractors and consultants, covering ownership, conflicts of interest with officials, prior contract performance, anti-corruption proceedings and adverse media. We report in English with source references so that procurement and compliance teams can document their decisions, and we flag where records are incomplete because of wartime restrictions.

faqs.q: Is ICAC arbitration in Kyiv still functioning?
faqs.a: The International Commercial Arbitration Court at the Ukrainian Chamber of Commerce and Industry continues to operate from Kyiv and to publish news and appoint arbitrators. Questions about seat, enforcement and court support are for counsel. We supply the factual research on parties, related companies and assets that counsel and tribunals often need.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have staff in Kyiv?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office, staff or address in Kyiv or elsewhere in Ukraine. Most work is desk-based research. Where on-the-ground steps are needed, we coordinate with qualified Ukrainian professionals acting lawfully with the client's counsel, plan for security conditions, and decline requests involving restricted records or covert methods.
